newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korea sets H2 foreign funds at $2.03 bln.
newsitem.headline: South Korea sets H2 foreign funds at $2.03 bln.

text.p: South Korea would allow investment trust companies to issue a total of $2.03 billion worth of beneficiary certificates for foreign investors in the second half of this year, the finance ministry said on Tuesday.
Beneficiary certificates are securities issued by trust companies, which have a guaranteed return on their investments in local stock and bond markets, on behalf of foreigners.
A ministry statement said the government earlier this year approved $1.97 billion worth of beneficiary certificates but $1.53 billion worth had not yet been issued.
The statement said the approved amount for the second half included the left-over.
Of the total $2.03 billion worth of certificates, trust companies were requested to invest $1.56 billion in the local stock market.
The statement said the move was aimed at boosting the Seoul bourse by expanding indirect foreign investment.

It also said the government had allowed newly established investment trust firms to issue beneficiary certificates abroad for investment in local bonds from the second half. Previously, the government allowed them to issue the certificates only for stock investment.
